feedback: Accepted. Format: all required headers present with correct syntax; FINAL_STATES is nonempty (u0), declared in STATES, and accepting for this task (the all-clear state after the current ring is silenced); INITIAL_STATE u0 declared. Reachability: both states are reachable — the first ring always comes within 30 steps, so u1 is entered every episode, and each successful toggle returns to u0. Compactness: two states is minimal; the u0/u1 split is what prevents the obvious exploit of rewarding no-op toggles on a silent siren. Persistent/event distinction: the persistent siren_ringing gates entry into u1, and the (u1, else) self-loop correctly avoids re-triggering while the siren keeps ringing; since the siren stops only via the switch, the machine in u1 guarantees the siren is ringing, so every (u1, switch_toggled) reward corresponds to a real siren being switched off — no farming possible. switch_toggled in u0 falls to else with no reward, so toggling silence earns nothing. Ordered coverage: explicit guards precede else in both states, and the per-state else self-loops cover all task-irrelevant propositions (holding_food, client_arrived, order_taken, food_prepared, order_served, food_fell, served_while_ringing). Regression: the recurring task (8–12 rings per episode) is handled by the explicit (u1, switch_toggled) -> u0 transition back to the accepting state. Reward safety/density: +1.0 per handled ring is sparse and schedule-bounded; the -0.01 waiting penalty is dense, bounded (worst case ~6.0 over 600 steps if the agent never acts, which is the intended pressure), and unspecified u0 transitions correctly default to 0 — notably no reward for the uncontrollable ring start itself. Minor benign corner: a toggle landing on the very step a ring starts (post-step siren already silent) goes unrewarded; this is acceptable, since rewarding it would require rewarding no-op toggles of a silent siren. Semantically faithful to 'whenever the siren goes off, switch it off again'.
